verses.sanskrit:
(इन्द्रवज्रा छन्द -)
कस्त्वं शिशो कस्य कुतोऽसि गन्ता
किं नाम ते त्वं कुत आगतोऽसि ।
एतन्मयोक्तं वद चार्भक त्वं
मत्प्रीतये प्रीति विवर्धनोऽसि ॥
verses.roman:
(indravajrā chanda -)
kastvaṃ śiśo kasya kuto'si gantā
kiṃ nāma te tvaṃ kuta āgato'si .
etanmayoktaṃ vada cārbhaka tvaṃ
matprītaye prīti vivardhano'si ..
verses.colloquial:
(indravajraa chanda -)
kastvam shisho kasya kuto'si gantaa
kim naama te tvam kuta aagato'si .
etanmayoktam vada chaarbhaka tvam
matpriitaye priiti vivardhano'si ..
verses.translation_reworded: Child, who are you? To whom do you belong? Where are you headed? What are you called, and where have you come from? Tell me all of this, little one. You have delighted my heart, and you are joy itself in living form.

verses.sanskrit:
हस्तामलक उवाच ।
नाहं मनुष्यो न च देव-यक्षौ
न ब्राह्मण-क्षत्रिय-वैश्य-शूद्राः ।
न ब्रह्मचारी न गृही वनस्थो
भिक्षुर्न चाहं निजबोध रूपः ॥
verses.roman:
hastāmalaka uvāca .
nāhaṃ manuṣyo na ca deva-yakṣau
na brāhmaṇa-kṣatriya-vaiśya-śūdrāḥ .
na brahmacārī na gṛhī vanastho
bhikṣurna cāhaṃ nijabodha rūpaḥ ..
verses.colloquial:
hastaamalaka uvaacha .
naaham manushyo na cha deva-yakshau
na braahmana-kshatriya-vaishya-shuudraah .
na brahmachaarii na grihii vanastho
bhikshurna chaaham nijabodha ruupah ..
verses.translation_reworded: Hastamalaka replied: I am not a human being or a divine being, not a yaksha or a spirit. I am not a Brahmin, Kshatriya, Vaishya, or Shudra. I am not a student, a householder, a forest-dweller, or a monk. I am pure awareness itself, whose very nature is Self-knowledge (nijabodha rupa).

verses.sanskrit:
(भुजङ्गप्रयात छन्द -)
निमित्तं मनश्चक्षुरादि प्रवृत्तौ
निरस्ताखिलोपाधिराकाशकल्पः ।
रविर्लोकचेष्टानिमित्तं यथा यः
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥१॥
verses.roman:
(bhujaṅgaprayāta chanda -)
nimittaṃ manaścakṣurādi pravṛttau
nirastākhilopādhirākāśakalpaḥ .
ravirlokaceṣṭānimittaṃ yathā yaḥ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 1..
verses.colloquial:
(bhujangaprayaata chanda -)
nimittam manashchakshuraadi pravrittau
nirastaakhilopaadhiraakaashakalpah .
ravirlokacheshtaanimittam yathaa yah
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 1..
verses.translation_reworded: As the sun drives the activities of all beings on earth, the Atma (Self) drives the working of the mind, the eye, and every other organ. Its nature is eternal Consciousness, and that is what I am. Apart from the limiting adjuncts (the body, mind, and sense-organs), I, the Self, am like space.

verses.sanskrit:
यमग्न्युष्णवन्नित्यबोध स्वरूपं
मनश्चक्षुरादीन्यबोधात्मकानि ।
प्रवर्तन्त आश्रित्य निष्कम्पमेकं
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥२॥
verses.roman:
yamagnyuṣṇavannityabodha svarūpaṃ
manaścakṣurādīnyabodhātmakāni .
pravartanta āśritya niṣkampamekaṃ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 2..
verses.colloquial:
yamagnyushnavannityabodha svaruupam
manashchakshuraadiinyabodhaatmakaani .
pravartanta aashritya nishkampamekam
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 2..
verses.translation_reworded: The mind, the eye, and the other organs are all insentient, and they function by relying on the Self. Heat is the very nature of fire, and in the same way eternal consciousness is the very nature of the Self, which never changes and is one alone (non-dual). I am that Self.

verses.sanskrit:
मुखाभासको दर्पणे दृश्यमानो
मुखत्वात् पृथक्त्वेन नैवास्ति वस्तु ।
चिदाभासको धीषु जीवोऽपि तद्वत्
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥३॥
verses.roman:
mukhābhāsako darpaṇe dṛśyamāno
mukhatvāt pṛthaktvena naivāsti vastu .
cidābhāsako dhīṣu jīvo'pi tadvat
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 3..
verses.colloquial:
mukhaabhaasako darpane drishyamaano
mukhatvaat prithaktvena naivaasti vastu .
chidaabhaasako dhiishu jiivo'pi tadvat
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 3..
verses.translation_reworded: A face seen in a mirror has no real existence apart from the face it reflects. Likewise the Jiva, merely the reflection of the Self or Pure Consciousness in the intellect (or mind), has no separate existence apart from the Self. I am that Self, whose nature is eternal consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा दर्पणाभाव आभासहानौ
मुखं विद्यते कल्पनाहीनमेकम् ।
तथा धी वियोगे निराभासको यः
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥ ४॥
verses.roman:
yathā darpaṇābhāva ābhāsahānau
mukhaṃ vidyate kalpanāhīnamekam .
tathā dhī viyoge nirābhāsako yaḥ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 4..
verses.colloquial:
yathaa darpanaabhaava aabhaasahaanau
mukham vidyate kalpanaahiinamekam .
tathaa dhii viyoge niraabhaasako yah
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 4..
verses.translation_reworded: Take away the mirror and the reflected face is gone; only the face remains, with no false appearance in the form of a reflection. In the same way, when the mind (the reflecting medium) is gone, the Atma stands free of every wrong notion the reflection had produced.

verses.sanskrit:
मनश्चक्षुरादेर्वियुक्तः स्वयं यो
मनश्चक्षुरादेर्मनश्चक्षुरादिः ।
मनश्चक्षुरादेरगम्यस्वरूपः
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥ ७॥
verses.roman:
manaścakṣurāderviyuktaḥ svayaṃ yo
manaścakṣurādermanaścakṣurādiḥ .
manaścakṣurāderagamyasvarūpaḥ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 5..
verses.colloquial:
manashchakshuraaderviyuktah svayam yo
manashchakshuraadermanashchakshuraadih .
manashchakshuraaderagamyasvaruupah
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 5..
verses.translation_reworded: I am the Self whose nature is eternal consciousness. It is distinct from the mind, the eye, and the other organs, yet it is the mind of the mind, the eye of the eye, the ear of the ear, and so on. Even so, the mind and the sense-organs cannot reach it.

verses.sanskrit:
य एको विभाति स्वतः शुद्धचेताः
प्रकाशस्वरूपोऽपि नानेव धीषु
शरावोदकस्थो यथा भानुरेकः
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥६॥
verses.roman:
ya eko vibhāti svataḥ śuddhacetāḥ
prakāśasvarūpo'pi nāneva dhīṣu
śarāvodakastho yathā bhānurekaḥ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 6..
verses.colloquial:
ya eko vibhaati svatah shuddhachetaah
prakaashasvaruupo'pi naaneva dhiishu
sharaavodakastho yathaa bhaanurekah
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 6..
verses.translation_reworded: Being self-luminous, the Self shines on its own for those whose minds have become entirely pure. It is one, yet in different intellects it looks like many separate things, just as the one sun looks like many when reflected in different pots of water. I am that Self, whose nature is eternal consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
यथाऽनेकचक्षुः-प्रकाशो रविर्न
क्रमेण प्रकाशीकरोति प्रकाश्यम् ।
अनेका धियो यस्तथैकः प्रबोधः
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥ ७॥
verses.roman:
yathā'nekacakṣuḥ-prakāśo ravirna
krameṇa prakāśīkaroti prakāśyam .
anekā dhiyo yastathaikaḥ prabodhaḥ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 7..
verses.colloquial:
yathaa'nekachakshuh-prakaasho ravirna
kramena prakaashiikaroti prakaashyam .
anekaa dhiyo yastathaikah prabodhah
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 7..
verses.translation_reworded: The sun gives light to every eye, and it does not show things to one person after another in turn; all eyes can see at the same moment. In the same way the one Self gives consciousness to all intellects at once.

verses.sanskrit:
विवस्वत् प्रभातं यथा रूपमक्षं
प्रगृह्णाति नाभातमेवं विवस्वान् ।
यदाभात आभासयत्यक्षमेकः
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥८॥
verses.roman:
vivasvat prabhātaṃ yathā rūpamakṣaṃ
pragṛhṇāti nābhātamevaṃ vivasvān .
yadābhāta ābhāsayatyakṣamekaḥ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 8..
verses.colloquial:
vivasvat prabhaatam yathaa ruupamaksham
pragrihnaati naabhaatamevam vivasvaan .
yadaabhaata aabhaasayatyakshamekah
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 8..
verses.translation_reworded: The eye sees clearly only what the sun lights up, and cannot see what the sun does not light. Yet the sun can enable the eye to see objects only because the Self illumines the sun itself.

verses.sanskrit:
यथा सूर्य एकोऽप्स्वनेकश्चलासु
स्थिरास्वप्यनन्यद्विभाव्यस्वरूपः
चलासु प्रभिन्नः सुधीष्वेक एव
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥ ९॥
verses.roman:
yathā sūrya eko'psvanekaścalāsu
sthirāsvapyananyadvibhāvyasvarūpaḥ
calāsu prabhinnaḥ sudhīṣveka eva
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 9..
verses.colloquial:
yathaa suurya eko'psvanekashchalaasu
sthiraasvapyananyadvibhaavyasvaruupah
chalaasu prabhinnah sudhiishveka eva
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 9..
verses.translation_reworded: One sun shows up as many reflections in various containers of water, some moving and some still, yet the nature of the water does not affect it. Similarly the one Self, though reflected in many ever-changing intellects, stays changeless and is not stained by their character.

verses.sanskrit:
घनच्छन्नदृष्टिर्घनच्छन्नमर्कम्
यथा निष्प्रभं मन्यते चातिमूढः ।
तथा बद्धवद्भाति यो मूढ-दृष्टेः
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥  १०॥
verses.roman:
ghanacchannadṛṣṭir ghanacchannamarkam
yathā niṣprabhaṃ manyate cātimūḍhaḥ .
tathā baddhavadbhāti yo mūḍha-dṛṣṭeḥ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 10..
verses.colloquial:
ghanacchannadrishtir ghanacchannamarkam
yathaa nishprabham manyate chaatimuudhah .
tathaa baddhavadbhaati yo muudha-drishteh
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 10..
verses.translation_reworded: A deeply ignorant person whose sight is blocked by a cloud supposes that the clouded sun has lost its brilliance. In the same way, to someone deluded by Avidya the Atma seems to be bound. I am that Atma, whose nature is eternal consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
समस्तेषु वस्तुष्वनुस्यूतमेकं
समस्तानि वस्तूनि यन्न स्पृशन्ति ।
वियद्वत्सदा शुद्धमच्छस्वरूपं
स नित्योपलब्धिस्वरूपोऽहमात्मा ॥ ११॥
verses.roman:
samasteṣu vastuṣvanusyūtamekaṃ
samastāni vastūni yanna spṛśanti .
viyadvatsadā śuddhamacchasvarūpaṃ
sa nityopalabdhisvarūpo'hamātmā .. 11..
verses.colloquial:
samasteshu vastushvanusyuutamekam
samastaani vastuuni yanna sprishanti .
viyadvatsadaa shuddhamacchasvaruupam
sa nityopalabdhisvaruupo'hamaatmaa .. 11..
verses.translation_reworded: One Self pervades everything in this universe, yet nothing can stain it. It is forever pure like space, untouched by the impurity of attachment and aversion, and immortal. I am that Self, whose nature is eternal consciousness.

verses.sanskrit:
उपाधौ यथा भेदता सन्मणीनां
तथा भेदता बुद्धिभेदेषु तेऽपि ।
यथा चन्द्रिकाणां जले चञ्चलत्वं
तथा चञ्चलत्वं तवापीह विष्णो ॥ १२॥
verses.roman:
upādhau yathā bhedatā sanmaṇīnāṃ
tathā bhedatā buddhibhedeṣu te'pi .
yathā candrikāṇāṃ jale cañcalatvaṃ
tathā cañcalatvaṃ tavāpīha viṣṇo .. 12..
verses.colloquial:
upaadhau yathaa bhedataa sanmaniinaam
tathaa bhedataa buddhibhedeshu te'pi .
yathaa chandrikaanaam jale chanchalatvam
tathaa chanchalatvam tavaapiiha vishno .. 12..
verses.translation_reworded: O all-pervading Lord! A crystal takes on different looks because of different limiting adjuncts, and You too seem different because You are reflected in different intellects. Reflections of the moon in different vessels of water move as the water moves, and You too seem to undergo change through Your association with different intellects.
